title: Affirmative possession review
focus: Mix the forms and sentence patterns already taught in this pack.

exercises.prompt: Choose the possessor form for “You have a ball.” Frame: “___ on pallo.” Use pallo (“a ball”) and on (“have/has”). Address one person.
exercises.explanation: Use sinulla, the possession form of sinä. The owner comes before fixed on.
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Personal possessor forms: form or meaning confused

optionFeedback.minulla: minulla identifies I as the owner; the requested owner is you.
optionFeedback.sinulla: Use sinulla, the possession form of sinä. The owner comes before fixed on.
optionFeedback.hänellä: hänellä identifies he as the owner; the requested owner is you.
optionFeedback.meillä: meillä identifies we as the owner; the requested owner is you.
optionFeedback.teillä: teillä identifies you as the owner; the requested owner is you.
optionFeedback.heillä: heillä identifies they as the owner; the requested owner is you.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: possessor + fixed on + one thing in its basic singular form

parts.role: possessor: the person who has the thing
parts.formation: sinä has the learned possession form sinulla; its -lla/-llä ending marks the possessor. Learn this pronoun form as a whole.
Olla means “to be”; possession uses its fixed on form with every owner, including we and they.
pallo stays in its basic singular form: one ball.

answerDiagnostics.category: Personal possessor forms: predictable form error
answerDiagnostics.explanation: The basic personal pronoun identifies a subject. Possession needs the learned -lla/-llä owner form shown by the lesson.
